findingSurfacedByTheNewGate.what: On its first post-fix run the boot smoke test did NOT pass. It failed later and differently: 'ENGINE_API_URL is required — cortex-api routes all reasoning through spine engine-api', thrown by validateEngineSpineEnvAtBoot at src/index.ts:178.
findingSurfacedByTheNewGate.whyItMatters: This is the discrimination proof. The instrument moved from a module-evaluation exit to a boot-validator refusal, which is only possible if the first defect was actually removed. A gate that reported pass at that moment would have been telling us nothing.
findingSurfacedByTheNewGate.disposition: Not an application defect. ENGINE_API_URL is set by the deploy workflow's --set-env-vars. The smoke env was incomplete and now supplies an unroutable host, chosen so the check cannot pass by reaching something real.
findingSurfacedByTheNewGate.secondMechanism: The alternative reading is that the fix broke engine-spine wiring. Rejected: the deploy workflow at .github/workflows/cloud-run-deploy.yml already sets ENGINE_API_URL in production, the validator only tests presence, and nothing in this lane touches engineSpineClient.ts.

adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.challenge: Does the boot smoke test prove production boots?
adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.answer: No, and it does not claim to. It proves the process reaches app.listen under a well-formed synthetic env with dummy secrets and an unreachable DATABASE_URL. A production-only failure caused by a wrong secret VALUE is out of its reach. Stated as scope, not mitigated.

adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.challenge: Could the graph guard be green while a CLI still reaches boot?
adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.answer: Yes, by three named routes: a bare workspace-package specifier (measured: all 13 *Cli.ts files in this repo are under artifacts/api-server/src and none is in a workspace package, so the gap is currently empty and reopens the moment one lands in lib/); a dynamic await import(), which is deliberately allowed because it does not evaluate at module load; and a require() or computed specifier. All three are written into the script header, not just into this artifact.

adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.challenge: Is the comment-and-string masking in the walker itself a risk?
adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.answer: It is the classic dead-gate hazard in reverse. The clean fixture deliberately contains a header that quotes the forbidden import verbatim plus an 'import type' from the same CLI, so the self-test fails if masking regresses in either direction. Both were exercised on every run above.

adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.challenge: Both controls are CI checks. Do they block anything?
adversarialReviewOfTheWorkSoFar.answer: No. This repo's main is not branch-protected, so under gate question three the honest answer today is that nothing fails. They are in the sixth state, advisory, per doctrine revision 7. Their evidentiary value is real and already banked; their protective value is nil until required status checks are enabled.
